questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: For me it was quite simple, I wanted to go somewhere that I could not go for just a weekend trip. I had the mindset that if I was going away, I might as well go as far away as possible.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I really enjoyed getting to know people from all over the world and experiencing everyday life in Australia. The academic level, however, was far below my expectations, which is why I only scored my overall experience 9.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I think it was fairly easy. There was a very nice environment for the international students and my specific campus, which meant that I was never in doubt about where to get the information that I needed. In general, they had built quite a great support system for new international students, so if you engage in the activities available, you should not have any trouble if you have any problems you need to talk to someone about - if you do not know who exactly to talk to, you would know who would know.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There were a lot of introductory activities in the first week, where I learned a lot about how the school system worked, how to find my way around campus and where I met a bunch of great people.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
I found my accommodation through the university's own webpage, where they recommended multiple accommodations, among others, the one I ended up choosing. The process was not that difficult, but they do fill up somewhat fast, so it is probably beneficial to look into accommodation as soon as you get your exchange spot because otherwise, it might get really expensive.

But after meeting people who lived at campus, I was kind of sad that I had not known this was an opportunity, because this seemed to be a lot more social than where I ended up living, even though the conditions were a bit worse.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Housing in Australia is very expensive even for a pretty scrappy room. Otherwise my experience was fine, I met some nice people where I lived, but it was not nearly as social as the accommodation on campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I think it was fairly easy. But I do think it was difficult to get in touch with them before I got to Australia. As soon as I was in Australia however, the process became much faster and easier as I could go and speak to them.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I registered online and was sent manuals that made it quite easy to know what to do.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I got sent a manual to follow, which made it easier, so I knew how to get through the process.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: 50/50 I would say. But I ended up with classes I thought was okay.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The classes are the most difficult to register for, since not only your host university but also the University of Copenhagen has to approve them. This can end up being quite time-consuming - so get started as fast as possible.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I do not think the academic level was as high as I have been used to from the University of Copenhagen - of course this can just be a coincidence due to the classes I took, but nevertheless it was my experience.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Most of the courses started almost from scratch with very little expectation to prior knowledge. I did not expect this from MA courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I think it was very much the same actually, but the papers we had to hand in during the trimester were not expected to be written in the same academic manner as I am used to.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Business Data Analytics
Portfolio Management
Personal Risk Management
Globalisation and Corporate Social Responsibility

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I think Portfolio Management and Globalisation and Corporate Social Responsibility were the ones I found most interesting and relevant for my studies in Denmark.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I do not think I experienced unexpected costs.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Housing was a lot more expensive than expected, otherwise it is pretty much the same price point as in Denmark.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were a lot of different clubs and sports to join - and you could often join club events without being a part of the club.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: There are a lot of activities hosted by Griffith Mates as well as SRC and GUPSA - these are really great and you get a really great price compared to if you had done those activities on your own.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: There are a lot of nice day trips to go on from the Brisbane area as well as the Gold Coast, so look some of these up! Also, if you have the time and money at some point, go see Uluru, it was without a doubt my greatest experience while I was in Australia.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I think it was very easy - there are so many people from all over the world in Australia, and Griffith is a very international university, so I experienced much more of this "international culture" than the Australian culture.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I mainly met international students, but they are the nicest most open people, so they are very easy to talk to.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I don't really think I can come up with any, I think it just made sense, especially in such an international environment.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The openness and how there was room for every possible culture, it made it easier to adapt and feel like you fit in and belong.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Go to every GUPSA/SRC/Griffith Mates event you can - it is great value for money, a lot of fun and you meet a lot of great people there!
2) Take advantage of all the great advisors and counsellors at Griffith - everything is free and they are so nice and helpful!
3) I think the thing that surprised me the most, was the way that your grade is made up from assessment throughout the semester, so I did not have any real exams. This was quite different from what I was used to and took some time to really understand, so be aware of that.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I think it is a very nice place, but if possible, take your classes at one of the larger campusses (Nathan or Gold Coast) as these are the ones with the greatest events and the most activities.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to know people from all over the world and learn about their lives and cultures.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Unfortunately, I was sick for a month while I was there, which was really hard, especially when you are so far from home. But Griffith has great counsellors and advisors who were able to help me, both in regards to how to see a doctor but also what to do with the assessments I had to hand in at a later time.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
